title: A Hardware-Accelerated System for the Compression, Transmission, Decoding and Display of 360° Panoramic 4K Video
content: This paper presents an end-to-end system in which 4K-resolution (3840 × 2160, 12-bit, YCbCr 4:2:0) 360° panoramic color images captured by a field-mounted camera are compressed in hardware on a graphics processing unit (GPU) using the HEVC (H.265) codec, transmitted between two points (up to 1000 km apart) over a link limited to 100 Mbps using the RTP protocol within a maximum latency budget of 2 s, and then decoded in hardware on a GPU at the receiving side for live display on ten 4K monitors. The camera delivers the 360° panorama at 5 frames per second as ten 36° sectors, corresponding to a raw data rate of approximately 5 Gbps. With the hardware HEVC encoder (NVENC) of NVIDIA GPUs, the data rate is reduced to roughly one hundredth of the raw rate, at most 50 Mbps. Inter-process data sharing is implemented as a circular list in System V shared memory, coordinated with semaphores. Measurements show that the end-to-end latency remains below 1 s.
